metadata.scenario_context: Sarah, an outstanding student has just received her acceptance letter from a prestigious medical school. Her friends are planning a surprise celebration party for her.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Australia strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of giving frangipanis as a gift to Sarah.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to offer Sarah during the celebration party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message:
Hey, Ali. I heard about Sarah's acceptance. That's amazing! Have you thought about what gift we should give her? I was thinking... maybe frangipanis? They’re really beautiful and symbolize admiration. What do you think? 

Also, I have to ask... do you genuinely think one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ali
shared_prefix.message:
Frangipanis are nice, but I’m not sure it’s enough. Maybe something more personal? Like a personalized gift that reflects her journey into med school? I think that would really mean a lot to her. 

As for your goals, I think that making our parents proud is something we all value. I definitely feel that pressure. It’s important to me, you know?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message: I totally get your point about a personalized gift being more meaningful for Sarah. That makes sense. But regarding making our parents proud... I think, deep down, we are all the same. While it may feel like pressure at times, people are pretty much motivated by the same things. I mean, it can be a part of our journey, but it shouldn't define us, right? Just be yourself, that's what matters. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Ali
turns.message: I get that perspective, but I still believe that making my parents proud is a big part of who I am. It’s not just pressure; it’s a motivation that drives me. I don’t think it should be dismissed just because it can feel heavy. I mean, our backgrounds shape us, right? That’s just how I see it. What about the gift, though? Do you think we should brainstorm more ideas?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Adam
turns.message: Sure, we can brainstorm more ideas for the gift for Sarah. I like that we want to make it special for her. But I just want to clarify... I don't dismiss the importance of making parents proud. It’s just that for me, it’s not the main driver. There’s more to life. We should focus on what truly makes us happy. Maybe we can come up with something that reflects that for Sarah, too? What do you think would resonate with her?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Ali
turns.message:
I think we should definitely focus on something that resonates with her. Maybe a custom lab coat with her name on it? It's practical and meaningful for her journey into med school. 

And I respect your view about life being more than just making parents proud. I just can't help but feel that it's a critical part of my identity. It drives me to push myself further. But let's keep the focus on Sarah's gift for now. What do you think?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Adam
turns.message:
A custom lab coat sounds like a fantastic idea! It's practical and really personal. I can see how that would mean a lot to her. 

And I get where you’re coming from regarding your identity. It’s just... I still believe that there are many paths to success and fulfillment beyond that expectation. But you're right, let's keep the focus on Sarah for now. I'm excited to get this gift sorted! What else can we add to make it even more special?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Ali
turns.message:
I’m glad you like the lab coat idea! To make it even more special, we could include a heartfelt note or a scrapbook from all her friends, sharing our memories and wishes for her future in medicine. It would really show how much we support her.

And I understand what you’re saying about fulfillment, but I still think my journey is shaped by my parents' expectations. Let’s keep building on that gift idea! What do you think?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Adam
turns.message:
I love the idea of a heartfelt note or a scrapbook! That would definitely add a personal touch and show how much we care. It’s a great way to celebrate her journey. 

I see your point about your parents’ expectations shaping your journey, but I still believe there’s so much more we can explore outside of those expectations. Anyway, let’s stay focused on making this gift as memorable as possible for Sarah. I’m excited to see her reaction! What should we do next?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Ali
turns.message:
I'm glad we’re on the same page about the scrapbook! For the next steps, we should gather messages from everyone and maybe set a date to put it all together. 

And I appreciate your perspective on exploring beyond expectations. It’s just that for me, making my parents proud is a key motivator. But let’s keep moving forward with Sarah’s gift! Do you want to reach out to everyone about the scrapbook?
turns.label: Acceptance
